intro.text: Mind the jars, dears. Oh, strangers! You wouldn't be passing the mill, would you? Hob's wife Merra has a fever and I daren't leave my pots.

options.text: We'll take your remedy to her.
Odran: "Your feverfew did wonders at the old temple last winter."

thanks.text: Bless you. Three drops in warm milk, morning and night. And tell Hob none of it is for him, the old goat.

odran.text: Brother Odran! I wondered where you'd got to. Still carrying half the temple's troubles on that broad back of yours?

waiting.text: Has Hob had the draught yet? The thatched cottage, west of the square.

after.text: Hob says Merra's fever broke in the night. You did a kind thing. Now, what can I do for you?
